title: Redwood discovery - Argus Systems - latency & throughput
summary: Introductory discovery to understand Argus's p95 latency targets, concurrency needs for real-time summarization and search, and whether Hosted, Dedicated or Private deployment is the right fit. Customer needs planned benchmarking (tokens/sec + p95), VPC connectivity for sensitive logs, and SOC2 compliance docs. SE to run a pilot benchmark in their VPC and share results.
topics: p95 latency targets (50-150ms for short responses; 500-800ms acceptable for long streaming)
concurrency and burst patterns (100 concurrent users, 1000 QPS bursts)
token/sec benchmarking and expected throughput per GPU
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private: security, latency, predictability
KV/prefix caching, batching, and quantization impact on throughput
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hi everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Maya, Redwood AE. With me is Liam, our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Sofia (Argus): Doing well, thanks. Quick heads up we're juggling a tight timeline — want to get performance numbers to decide on Dedicated vs Private.
[00:14] Liam (Redwood SE): Great — we'll focus on p95 targets, concurrency, and the benchmarking steps. Can you run through your current stack?
[00:23] Rajesh (Argus): Sure — we run a microservice on k8s, models hosted on a mix of in-house GPU infra and some managed endpoints. For prod we want sub-200ms p95 for short prompts (<= 64 tokens) and <600ms for longer streaming responses. Concurrency baseline is 100 sustained users with spikes to 1k for 2-3 minutes.
[00:40] Maya: That's helpful. Are you planning request streaming to reduce tail latency?
[00:44] Sofia: Yes, for the UI we stream token-by-token for chat and summarization. But for some batch rerank jobs we accept higher latency.
[00:50] Liam: Streaming helps perceived latency — you can surface first tokens in 50-80ms while full completion might be 300-500ms depending on token count. For p95 we look at end-to-end: network, model decode, and postprocessing.
[01:10] Emily (CTO): Important point: security — we need VPC peering or an on-prem option because of regulated PII. SOC2 Type II is required and we need KMS for customer-managed keys.
[01:20] Maya: Understood. We have Redwood Private with a customer-managed control plane and KMS/HSM integrations; Dedicated also offers reserved capacity and private network connectivity options. We'll share the SOC2 + security pack.
[01:30] Rajesh: For benchmarking, we want tokens/sec numbers for our median prompt (approx 120 tokens) and max token cases (1k tokens) — and how quantization affects throughput. Also curious how KV cache and prefix caching changes throughput for chat sessions.
[01:42] Liam: Good — rough numbers: on a single A100-class GPU with optimized kernels, you might see ~150-400 tokens/sec for 120-token runs depending on precision (fp16 vs int8) and model size. With q4_0/q4_1 style quantization you get ~1.5-2x throughput at modest quality tradeoffs. KV cache benefits multi-turn: warm cache can cut decode work significantly, improving p95.
[02:05] Sofia: Those ranges are wide — can we get concrete p95 examples?
[02:09] Liam: Sure. Example: 13B model on Dedicated, fp16, 1 token stream-first-byte might be 30-50ms, end-to-end completion for 120 tokens at ~250-350ms p95 at single request concurrency. With batching and 8-way concurrency on the same instance you can push tokens/sec up but p95 for single user may increase.
[02:29] Maya: So it's the classic latency vs throughput tradeoff — Dedicated gives you predictable throughput and isolated pools, Hosted is simpler but subject to multi-tenant variability, Private gives you full control and lowest network hops if co-located.
[02:44] Rajesh: For our UI real-time experience we need p95 under 200ms for 64 tokens; if we can't meet that on Hosted we'll evaluate Dedicated with reserved GPU pool in our region or Private in our VPC. Any network added hops from Private?
[02:58] Liam: With Private deployed in your VPC or on-prem, network hops are minimized — so you'll get lower network latency. We also offer local model variants optimized for lower-latency kernels, and routing policies to hit lower-latency pools.
[03:12] Sofia: About concurrency — we see 100 concurrent active chats, but 1k users hitting the system during release windows. How does Redwood handle bursts?
[03:20] Liam: Dedicated supports burst capacity and autoscaling policies; you can reserve baseline GPUs and allow warm burst pools. Hosted will scale but subject to regional capacity. For strict SLOs we recommend Dedicated or Private so you can reserve capacity.
[03:33] Rajesh: Any guidance on batch sizes vs latency?
[03:36] Liam: Batching improves throughput but hurts single-request latency. We recommend adaptive batching: small micro-batches for real-time routes (batch size 1-4) and larger batch sizes for asynchronous workloads. Auto-tuning can help.
[03:50] Maya: Can we talk about metrics you'll want to see from the benchmark?
[03:53] Sofia: p50, p95, p99 latencies, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, cost per 1M tokens, and warm vs cold KV cache numbers. Also drop-in comparisons between fp16 and quantized profiles.
[04:08] Liam: We'll provide a benchmark playbook that measures those. We'll run token/sec synthetic tests and replay your production traces for p95 and concurrency. For streaming, we'll measure first-token latency separately and end-to-end completion p95.
[04:22] Rajesh: How do you replay traces? Does Redwood accept request traces with user IDs stripped?
[04:26] Liam: Yes, replay with anonymized traces. We have a trace-runner that preserves timing and concurrency patterns. We can run it in-hosted sandbox or in your VPC depending on data sensitivity.
[04:37] Emily: Cost is also key — rough order of magnitude for Dedicated vs Hosted for our projected 200M tokens/month?
[04:44] Maya: We'll send a tailored pricing sheet, but generally Dedicated lowers unit cost at scale due to reserved capacity; Hosted is higher per-token but minimal ops overhead. We'll include cost modelling in the benchmark deliverable.
[04:58] Sofia: Security checklist — SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs retention, KMS, SOC2, data residency. Can you send the security pack and integration docs?
[05:07] Maya: Yes — I'll attach our security pack and a short integration guide for VPC/private deployments.
[05:12] Rajesh: For the pilot we'd like an SE-run benchmark in our VPC. Timeline: can you do that next week? We want to present results to the execs in two weeks.
[05:21] Liam: We can run a focused pilot next week — we'll need an anonymized trace, access to a staging VPC, and a point of contact for connectivity. We'll scope it to 2-3 model variants (13B fp16, 13B q4, and a 30B fp16) and measure p95 for 64/120/1k token scenarios plus streaming first-token.
[05:40] Sofia: Sounds good. Any gotchas we should be aware of?
[05:43] Liam: Watch out for network egress and packaging — big batches affect KV cache warming. Also quantization can change output distribution slightly; we'll include quality checks in the replay.
[05:53] Maya: Let's talk next steps and owners.
[05:55] Rajesh: Quick note — some of our internal names got garbled in calendar invites, but the participants are correct.
[06:01] Maya: Noted.
[06:02] Emily: One more question: does Redwood provide per-route SLOs and automatic fallback to smaller models if a node is overloaded?
[06:09] Liam: Yes — routing policies and automatic fallback are supported; you can define per-route model pins and fallback chains to ensure availability. We'll demo that in the pilot.
[06:18] Maya: OK, recap: Redwood to send security pack, pricing sheet, and benchmark playbook today; SE to run pilot in Argus staging VPC next week using anonymized traces; deliver results in ~7 business days; follow-up meeting to review and decide Dedicated vs Private.
[06:32] Sofia: Correct — and please include explicit numbers for p95 targets and tokens/sec per GPU so we can include in our capacity planning.
[06:40] Maya: Will do. Thanks everyone.
[06:42] Rajesh: Thanks.
[06:44] Emily: Thanks all.
[06:45] [call ends]

Maya: share pricing sheet for Hosted/Dedicated/Private (today)
Liam: run SE benchmark in Argus staging VPC (next week) — 3 model variants, p95+tokens/sec
